metadata.ontology_name: Cartenza Affinity Tag Ontology v0.2.2 + Schema Boundary Amendment v0.3.1
metadata.notes: Controlled ontology candidate with uplift added and stricter sparse tagging rules. Not graph-wide production metadata.
metadata.status: ontology and sparse rules approved; output schema conditionally approved for graph-wide tagging after PM acceptance; not approved for runtime ingestion
metadata.example_song_ids_policy: Example song IDs are illustrative only. If an example appears inconsistent with the tag definition, follow the tag definition, not the example.
metadata.alias_leakage_policy: Any retagging output using aliases instead of canonical tags fails QA.
metadata.schema_boundary_policy: Core dimensions attach to canonical song/recording truth; social_context and routing_caution attach primarily to membership_context_overlays.

dimensions.definition: Voice, delivery, group-vocal identity, vocal stance, vocal persona, or explicit instrumental/no-vocal identity when vocal performance is not the route-bearing feature.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Large foreground vocal; includes soul belt, pop power vocal, theatrical belting, and operatic force when the voice is a primary attraction.
canonical_tags.use_when: The vocal scale, range, projection, or climactic belt is route-bearing.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use merely because the singer is famous or technically skilled.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Close, private, restrained, or fragile vocal presence.
canonical_tags.use_when: The route depends on closeness, vulnerability, or small-room vocal affect.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic ballads with large or polished vocals.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Audibly rough, torn, frayed, or strained vocal character.
canonical_tags.use_when: Roughness or strain is part of the expressive identity.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for merely energetic or loud vocals unless the surface is actually ragged.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Conversational, direct, talk-like, understated, or unornamented delivery.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song’s trust signal comes from directness or speech-like delivery.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for rap flow unless the central route is spoken directness rather than rhythmic flow.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Emotionally withheld, stylized, deadpan, or coolly controlled delivery.
canonical_tags.use_when: The vocal stance is detached, icy, blasé, or intentionally non-demonstrative.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for weak singing or low affect that is not aesthetically purposeful.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Pressed, shouted, bratty, rushed, confrontational, or high-urgency delivery.
canonical_tags.use_when: Vocal urgency is central to energy, rebellion, or pressure.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for any fast song by default.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Exposed, emotionally naked, shame-bearing, or confessional performance.
canonical_tags.use_when: The vocal identity carries confession, wound, or self-exposure.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for general sadness unless the performance itself feels exposed.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Tight harmonies, blended group singing, or arranged vocal stacking.
canonical_tags.use_when: Harmony blend is route-bearing across pop, doo-wop, folk, country, rock, or vocal standards.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for background vocals that do not shape the song identity.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Group, choir, cast, chant, congregation, or crowd identity.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song works as a shared vocal object or collective vocal surface.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for a solo lead with incidental backing vocals.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Clearly processed, filtered, vocoded, tuned, or digitally mediated vocal identity.
canonical_tags.use_when: Processing is central to texture, persona, or genre crossing.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use when production is polished but the vocal itself is naturalistic.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Vocal delivery as rhythmic engine: rap, chant-flow, percussive speech, or flow-forward performance.
canonical_tags.use_when: The vocal rhythm drives the track.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary melody with a steady beat.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Vocal is inseparable from character, persona, parody, camp, or theatrical mask.
canonical_tags.use_when: The route must understand a constructed persona or character delivery.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for any singer with a recognizable style unless persona/character is the point.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: No vocal or vocal is not central; instrumental timbre/motif/performance substitutes for vocal identity.
canonical_tags.use_when: Instrumental works, scores, jazz features, dance instrumentals, or songs where the lead motif is the “voice.”
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use as a lazy fallback when a vocal actually carries the song.

dimensions.definition: Central emotional or thematic material, independent of whether the song is “liked.”

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Desire for union, yearning, waiting, distance, or unresolved romantic pull.
canonical_tags.use_when: Romantic wanting is the main emotional engine.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for every love song; use more specific tags when grief, bliss, or desire dominates.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Romantic loss, rejection, breakup ache, betrayal, or devastated attachment.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song’s romance is defined by hurt or rupture.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for light flirtation or generalized longing.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Erotic pull, attraction, seduction, bodily desire, or nocturnal sensuality.
canonical_tags.use_when: Desire or sexual charge is route-bearing.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic romance without sensual/erotic charge.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Estrangement, isolation, dislocation, social unease, or identity pressure.
canonical_tags.use_when: The emotional route is separation, not just sadness.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use as a blanket alternative/indie tag.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Anger, fury, attack, revenge, or self-directed violence/abrasion.
canonical_tags.use_when: Anger is a primary emotional driver.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use merely because guitars are loud.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Defiance, protest, anti-authority, political refusal, or social challenge.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song’s stance is oppositional or resistant.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary youthful energy without a defiant stance.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Joy, release, triumph, group pleasure, dancing together, or party energy.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song functions emotionally as release or celebration.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for any uptempo track by default.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Memory, old times, childhood, home, pastness, seasonal recurrence, or sentimental return.
canonical_tags.use_when: Backward-looking feeling is central.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use solely because the song is old.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Prayer, longing for God/transcendence, surrender, awe, redemption, or spiritual lift.
canonical_tags.use_when: Spiritual or transcendent desire is the point.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic uplift unless it is spiritually framed.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Self-construction, swagger, star persona, braggadocio, myth-making, victory pose.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song builds a persona or triumphal self-image.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary confidence without mythic or performative self-presentation.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Comedy, parody, absurdity, knowingly ridiculous premises, or camp humor.
canonical_tags.use_when: Humor/absurdity is part of how the song should route.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for unintentionally silly songs unless the context is camp-sensitive.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Death, bereavement, lament, elegy, historical trauma, or communal grief.
canonical_tags.use_when: The emotional center is mourning rather than romance or melancholy.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for vague sadness.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Threat, fear, menace, paranoia, doom, or ominous tension.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song creates danger or dread as a key bridge.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use merely because the song is minor-key.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Release-oriented, emotionally rising, aspirational, or cathartic positive turn that is not simply celebration, romance, nostalgia, or self-mythology.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use when the song’s central emotional motion is upward release, resilience, empowerment, or cathartic lift.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for every upbeat song; celebration covers party/joy, spiritual_yearning covers devotional reach, and self_mythology covers triumphal persona-making.

dimensions.definition: Instrumentation, production feel, surface, density, and sound-world.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Guitar is central to the track’s identity, but not necessarily distorted.
canonical_tags.use_when: Guitar timbre/riff/strum is a primary route-bearing surface.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for incidental guitar in a production-dominant pop song.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Distortion, fuzz, crunch, noise, or abrasive guitar surface.
canonical_tags.use_when: Distorted guitar texture creates pressure, bite, or heaviness.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for clean rock guitar.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Acoustic, small-room, sparse, or close-grained instrumentation.
canonical_tags.use_when: The acoustic surface creates intimacy or plainspokenness.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for all country/folk songs automatically.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Piano carries harmony, hook, rhythm, or emotional identity.
canonical_tags.use_when: Piano is the lead structural or emotional instrument.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for background piano decoration.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Strings/orchestra/symphonic lift or swelling arrangement.
canonical_tags.use_when: Orchestral scale or string arrangement materially shapes emotion/form.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for tiny string pads without route impact.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Horns, brass, sax sections, mariachi horns, or punchy horn architecture.
canonical_tags.use_when: Horn writing is a connective texture across soul, jazz, Latin, pop, or rock.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for a single incidental horn unless it defines the hook.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Synths, electronic sheen, programmed timbres, or synthetic lead/bass surfaces.
canonical_tags.use_when: Synthetic timbre is a core part of the song’s identity.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use merely because a modern record has digital production.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Bass, sub-bass, down-tuned weight, or low-end pressure is central.
canonical_tags.use_when: The body-force or menace comes from low end.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for any bassline that is simply present.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Band-in-room, live, rough, garage, or unvarnished ensemble force.
canonical_tags.use_when: The sound-world is physical ensemble presence rather than studio polish.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for every rock band.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Clean, glossy, radio-ready, highly controlled studio surface.
canonical_tags.use_when: Polish is route-relevant, especially for pop, adult, worship, R&B, or soft-rock objects.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use as praise or criticism; pair with emotion/form tags.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Production is architected as a world: layers, transitions, spatial design, arrangement drama.
canonical_tags.use_when: The recording’s built environment is part of the composition.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for generic polish.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Shadowy, nocturnal, hazy, narcotic, ominous, or enveloping atmosphere.
canonical_tags.use_when: Mood/atmosphere is the connective texture.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use solely because lyrics are sad.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Samples, loops, collage, beat-making, or repurposed audio as central texture.
canonical_tags.use_when: Sample/loop logic materially shapes the song.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary repetition without sample/collage identity.

dimensions.definition: Movement, pulse, groove, bodily feel, pacing, and energy shape.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Direct backbeat, stomp, claps, or blunt physical pulse.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song is carried by a simple bodily backbeat/stomp.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for every 4/4 track.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Forward-motion eighth-note drive or propulsion.
canonical_tags.use_when: The route depends on relentless forward motion.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for merely medium-tempo rock.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Tight, repeated, body-centered groove that locks in.
canonical_tags.use_when: Groove continuity is the central bodily feel.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for all dance tracks; use dancefloor when public dance function dominates.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Public dance orientation, club motion, disco/house/pop-dance utility, or four-on-floor lift.
canonical_tags.use_when: The track routes as dance music or danceable pop.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for any song that merely has rhythm.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Offbeat, stuttered, syncopated, chopped, or displaced rhythmic motion.
canonical_tags.use_when: Syncopation or rhythmic interruption is route-bearing.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary backbeat swing.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Slow, deliberate, ballad-paced, or steady emotional pacing.
canonical_tags.use_when: Pacing matters more than groove or propulsion.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for slow songs that are actually slow-burn builds.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Gradual accumulation, long arc, trance build, or cinematic growth.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song’s payoff depends on cumulative build.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for any long song without a build arc.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Build toward shared chorus, lift, chant, or stadium-scale release.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song is structured toward collective lift.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for private/intimate choruses.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Verse/chorus contrast, loud arrival, drop, or cathartic eruption.
canonical_tags.use_when: The chorus/drop explosion is the body event.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for songs with consistent dynamics.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Physical impact energy suited to punk/metal/hardcore/alt-rock impact.
canonical_tags.use_when: The body feel is collision, slam, or aggressive release.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for merely loud classic rock.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Sparse, reduced, minimal, or barely-there pulse.
canonical_tags.use_when: The track routes through restraint or minimal motion.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for empty arrangements if rhythm is not meaningful.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Swing, shuffle, two-step, boogie, train beat, or rolling rhythmic feel.
canonical_tags.use_when: The rhythmic feel is swung/rolling rather than straight.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use as a country/blues blanket tag.

dimensions.definition: Song architecture, object type, performance container, and format. Social use-case belongs in social_context, not here.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Compact song built around hook, verse/chorus craft, radio legibility, or single-object impact.
canonical_tags.use_when: The object is best understood as a crafted single.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use alone to build edges; pair with emotion/texture/rhythm tags.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Song is best interpreted inside a larger album-world or immersive record environment.
canonical_tags.use_when: The track’s route value depends on its album/container context.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for any album track by default.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Song tells a story, testimony, message, scene, or character arc.
canonical_tags.use_when: Narrative content is central to form.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for lyrics that merely contain events.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Song functions as an anthem, scene marker, or large shared cultural anchor.
canonical_tags.use_when: The form is built for collective recognition or anthem-scale deployment.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use simply because a song is famous.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Song is heavily organized around repeatable, high-impact hook/chorus machinery.
canonical_tags.use_when: The chorus/hook engine dominates form.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for all pop singles.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Song’s architecture is organized around a riff or repeated instrumental hook.
canonical_tags.use_when: The riff is the formal anchor.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for any guitar song.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Track is built as a dance/club object rather than simply pop with a beat.
canonical_tags.use_when: DJ/club/dance structure matters to form.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use when social context is danceable but form is radio-pop.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Song/recording is materially tied to film, TV, stage, score, or screen narrative.
canonical_tags.use_when: Its object identity is soundtrack/score/cinematic.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for songs merely used in many movies.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Standard, canonical vocal/jazz tune, or interpretation-oriented object.
canonical_tags.use_when: The route should account for performance tradition and interpretive versions.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for every old song.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Suite-like, theatrical, conceptual, dramatic-scene, or multi-section composition.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song is not just verse/chorus; concept or staged architecture matters.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for any song from a concept album.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Extended performance, soloing, groove exploration, or instrumental feature vehicle.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song is route-useful as a performance/groove vehicle.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for every instrumental.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Novelty, camp, parody, children’s, meme, or joke-adjacent object.
canonical_tags.use_when: The object type itself demands novelty/camp handling.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for unusual songs unless novelty/camp is the actual container.

dimensions.definition: Likely social/use setting or contextual container. These are not risk judgments and not preference claims.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Social party, bar, house party, reception, or shared fun setting.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song is strongly associated with party use.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for all celebratory songs; use celebration in emotion_theme if no social container is implied.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: General dance/social dancing context outside strictly club form.
canonical_tags.use_when: People are expected to move/dance socially to it.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use when rhythm is danceable but context is private listening.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Karaoke, singalong, bar-room belting, or communal amateur performance.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song has singalong/karaoke gravity.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use merely because the chorus is catchy.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Wedding, first dance, reception, or romantic ceremony context.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song is strongly tied to wedding/romance ceremony use.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for all love songs.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Holiday, Christmas, seasonal ritual, or annual recurrence context.
canonical_tags.use_when: Seasonal use materially shapes routing.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use only because song mentions a season.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Family listening, children’s context, household-safe shared object, or cross-age familiarity.
canonical_tags.use_when: Family/shared setting is central.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use as a moral approval tag.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Congregational, devotional, church, faith community, or worship setting.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song is likely used or understood in religious practice/community.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for secular songs with spiritual metaphors.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Film, TV, musical, trailer, score, Disney, or screen-associated listening context.
canonical_tags.use_when: Screen/stage context shapes expectations.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use when the song is simply cinematic in production.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Oldies, childhood, throwback, generational memory, or context-first familiarity.
canonical_tags.use_when: The route must account for memory/context rather than pure affinity.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use solely due to release age.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Stadium, chant, ritual, march, service, mass participation, or collective repetition context.
canonical_tags.use_when: The song works as a ritual/shared participation object.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for solo listening anthems unless participation is central.

dimensions.definition: Special handling warnings for mission sequencing, route construction, feedback interpretation, and whiplash control. These are not moral judgments.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Accessible entry point into a family, archetype, or route.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use when song can safely introduce a route without over-testing the listener.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use as a synonym for mass-recognition; the song must also be route-legible.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Massively familiar song whose familiarity may swamp true affinity signal.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use when recognition/context may distort user feedback.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for merely well-known songs; reserve for potentially signal-distorting anchors.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Abrupt sound/context/emotional jump likely to require sequencing care.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use for extreme metal, hyperpop, abrasive noise, odd novelty, or sudden cross-context jumps.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for ordinary genre difference.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Looks adjacent by genre/surface but may fail because the underlying affinity function differs.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use where graph proximity could misroute users.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for all boundary songs; specify the false-nearby concern in notes.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Needs explanatory setup, mission framing, or surrounding context before presentation.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use where user response depends heavily on expectation-setting.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use simply because the song is obscure.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Meaning/use changes strongly by setting: party, worship, holiday, family, movie, nostalgia, meme, etc.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use when feedback should be interpreted through context before taste inference.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use as a vague uncertainty label.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Explicit lyrical/content context may affect routing, family setting, or tester comfort.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use for explicit sexual/violent/profane material when route planning needs awareness.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use as value judgment.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Camp/theater/persona framing can work or fail depending on user tolerance.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use for glam, Broadway, novelty, hyperpop, theatrical pop, or exaggerated persona objects.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for all theatrical songs; use when camp sensitivity is specifically relevant.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Potentially cloying, manipulative, maudlin, or soft-prestige emotional surface.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use where emotional directness may become too sweet or overwrought for some routes.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for sincere emotional songs by default.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: May sound like genre cosplay, revival costume, pastiche, or scene appliance.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use when the surface imitates a style and authenticity/function may be questioned.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for genuine genre participation.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: Joke/meme/children’s/novelty context may overpower musical affinity.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use when novelty can distort feedback or route logic.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use for playful but musically robust songs unless novelty dominates.

canonical_tags.analyst_note: A song/album/artist may work as a singular exception without validating nearby graph territory.
canonical_tags.use_when: Use for highly specific objects whose success should not generalize broadly.
canonical_tags.do_not_use_when: Do not use whenever something is simply excellent.

governance_rules: Only canonical tags go into runtime payloads; aliases and analyst notes remain tooling-only.
No family-wide blanket tagging: a song receives a tag only when the song itself carries that feature.
Genre, scene, era, recognition, and family metadata should not be duplicated as affinity tags unless they change route behavior.
Every production tag should be paired with at least one emotion, rhythm, form, social_context, or routing_caution tag before it is used to form an edge.
Routing cautions are operational warnings, not evaluative judgments.
Aliases are dimension-scoped; the same string may appear as analyst language in multiple places, but retagging output must use only canonical tags.
Example song IDs are illustrative only. If an example appears inconsistent with the tag definition, follow the tag definition, not the example.
Any output using aliases instead of canonical tags fails QA.
Use reason-coded review fields: recording_identity_unclear, tag_definition_ambiguous, missing_tag_candidate, social_context_unclear, routing_caution_unclear, over_tagged, under_tagged.
Sparse production-simulation default target: 5–8 total canonical tags per song.
9–10 tags are allowed only when the song is genuinely multi-context, bridge-heavy, or routing-sensitive; those cases should be rare and reviewable.
Empty dimensions are allowed. Do not tag every dimension just to satisfy output shape.
Default maximum remains 1–2 primary tags per dimension. Prefer one primary tag in ordinary cases.
safe_gateway is not a default; use only when the song actively helps sequence into a route.
context_dependent is not a default caution; use only when social/use-case context materially changes routing.
